A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MODNAS. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original architecture-search experiments on NAS-Bench-201, ImageNet-1k and WMT’14 En-De, including hardware comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original search experiments and reports expanded baseline comparisons and new GPT-based language-modeling results, including predictor-based evaluations in Appendix J.4.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same four components, preference conditioning, ReinMax sampling and MGD updates. GPT experiments adapt the existing framework to another search space. The frozen-supernetwork option emphasized in v2 already appears in v1 Figure 22.

E1.justification: v2 adds autoregressive language modeling on OpenWebText using the GPT-S space from HW-GPT-Bench, evaluating perplexity and energy across eight GPU types. This substantially extends task and hardware coverage beyond the retained image-classification and machine-translation experiments.

E2.justification: v1 primarily evaluates RS, RHPN, HELP and HAT. v2 adds extensive actual comparisons with methods including NSGA-II, qEHVI, MO-ASHA, MO-RE, CMA-ES, LaMOO combinations and scalarization-based Bayesian optimization. HELP also enters the NAS constraint analysis but disappears from the reported HAT comparisons.

E3.justification: v1’s 24-sample random-search comparisons expand into budgeted searches and 50-evaluation NAS-Bench-201 tests. v2 specifies larger HAT baseline budgets, 192-hour OFA baseline searches using an accuracy predictor, and a new GPT evaluation protocol. Frozen OFA weights become the main setting, having been supplementary in v1. HAT runtime statements are not fully reconciled with Table 4.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial search-efficiency and budget-sensitivity analyses through evaluation-count curves and doubled-budget comparisons (Figures 4, 16 and 19). The separate MobileNetV3 0.2-constraint analysis in v1 Figure 21 is absent. Existing sampler, gradient-update and device-count ablations remain, while the frozen-supernetwork variant moves into the main evaluation.

E5.justification: Both versions report means of three independent NAS-Bench-201 searches and already use shaded variability plots. v2 introduces no explicit increase in runs, seed disclosure, new uncertainty definition or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive baseline scores, budget curves and GPT Pareto fronts. Whereas MODNAS led v1’s displayed HAT comparator set, v2 Figure 23 reports Xeon BLEU-based hypervolume of 0.81 for NSGA-II versus 0.80 for MODNAS. Figure 9 newly reports average OFA hypervolume of 0.76 for MODNAS versus 0.74 for LS-BO. These are expanded or revised comparisons, not established same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: The Pareto definitions, bi-level formulation, MGD dual problem, Frank-Wolfe reasoning, objective penalty and normalization are substantively retained. Mathematical material is condensed or relocated; added sampler pseudocode documents existing procedures rather than introducing new theory or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion extend the empirical applicability claim from three search spaces and two tasks to four spaces and three tasks, explicitly including decoder-only language modeling. The central claims of single-search Pareto profiling and zero-shot device transfer remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds discussion of when single-objective constrained optimization is useful, interprets the GPT results as evidence of effectiveness beyond convex Pareto fronts, and introduces environmental implications in Appendix A. These extend the interpretation while retaining the earlier mechanism and scalability explanations.

D1.justification: v2 adds GPT predictor architecture, architecture encodings, hardware splits and training configurations; identifies SyneTune as the baseline implementation source; and provides pipeline runtime breakdowns in Table 4. Appendix C adds explicit sampler pseudocode. The original three spaces’ hyperparameter settings and MODNAS code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The dedicated baseline discussion in v2 Appendix D substantially expands positioning against evolutionary and Bayesian multi-objective optimization. New references include LaMOO, qEHVI, MO-ASHA, random-scalarization Bayesian optimization and HW-GPT-Bench. This goes beyond citation-format changes and broadens the comparison with prior research.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites and reorganizes the explanation: the main hypernetwork description is simplified, detailed mathematics and sampler descriptions move to appendices, computational complexity becomes Section 4.4, and the appendices are restructured. Introductory and related-work paragraphs are also substantially edited.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive figure and table rearrangement. v2 adds a simplified architecture overview, budget curves, GPT plots and a runtime table, expands comparison legends, and replaces the main OFA radar with aggregate and per-device bar charts. Figure 6 introduces a device-caption mismatch: Eyeriss in the caption versus gold_6226 in the plot.

improvement.justification: The expanded evaluations address v1’s important weakness of relying mainly on random and constrained-search comparators. Direct MOO comparisons and budget-sensitivity tests substantially strengthen the evidence for the central efficiency claim, while the GPT task and additional implementation details broaden its assessment. Removal of the OFA constraint analysis, inconsistent runtime accounting and overly broad HAT superiority wording are drawbacks, but the stronger empirical scrutiny provides a substantial net improvement.
